label: Heart
function: Pumps blood through the body and delivers oxygen and nutrients to every organ.
spaceRisks: Fluid shifts toward the head in microgravity and change the load on the heart.
Long-term radiation exposure may raise cardiovascular risk.
Without regular exercise the heart muscle weakens (cardiovascular deconditioning).

label: Brain
function: Controls thinking, mood, sleep and every other system of the body.
spaceRisks: Sleep disruption from light cycles, noise and schedules.
Isolation, confinement and distance from Earth affect behavioral health.
Fluid shifts and radiation may affect brain function and vision.

label: Lungs
function: Bring oxygen into the blood and remove carbon dioxide.
spaceRisks: Raised CO2 or low O2 in a closed cabin lowers blood oxygen.
Dust and particles stay airborne in microgravity and irritate the airways.

label: Bones
function: Support the body, protect organs and store calcium.
spaceRisks: Bone density is lost in microgravity without loading and exercise.
Calcium released from bones can raise the risk of kidney stones.

label: Muscles
function: Produce movement and keep posture and strength.
spaceRisks: Muscles that fight gravity on Earth weaken quickly in space.
Daily resistance exercise is needed to limit strength loss.

label: Immune system
spaceRisks: Spaceflight changes immune function and can reactivate dormant viruses.
Infections spread easily in a small closed cabin.

label: Metabolism
function: Turns food into energy and keeps blood sugar in balance.
spaceRisks: Stress, changed diet and low activity can affect blood sugar.
Inadequate nutrition is one of the risks of long missions.
